issues.title: Missing contact-value shift in the zero-order-dependent stability proof
issues.claim: At the positive maximum of u_k-Q_epsilon, the printed proof evaluates F at zero-order value Q_epsilon instead of u_k.
issues.assumptions_verified: Continuous smooth F(M,p,z,x)=(tr M)^5+z is elliptic (monotone in PSD matrices), not uniformly elliptic; no uniform ellipticity or zero-order properness is stipulated. u_k=u=Q=0 on B1 are viscosity solutions, uniformly convergent; Q touches; annulus estimate holds for epsilon<1/4.
issues.complete_check: In n=4, x_epsilon=0,m_epsilon=epsilon^4,epsilon=1/65536. Printed F=(8epsilon)^5-epsilon^4=-epsilon^4/2<0. Correct touching test Q_epsilon+m_epsilon=epsilon|x|^2 gives +(epsilon^4)/2. Negative printed value persists for all 0<epsilon<8^-5.
issues.counterevidence: The actual compactness application uses G_H(M)=tr(M+H)-sqrt(2+|M+H|^2), independent of the zero-order variable. Adding a constant does not change this operator. The stability lemma itself remains true.
issues.repair: Use m_epsilon=max(u_k-Q_epsilon), phi_epsilon=Q_epsilon+m_epsilon and evaluate the zero-order argument at u_k(x_epsilon). 0<m_epsilon<=||u_k-u||_infinity+epsilon^4 ->0. Pass to the limit by continuity; analogous lower-test argument.
issues.core_impact: No broken dependency to the main Hessian estimate, conditional higher-dimensional estimate or dimension-four viscosity regularity has been demonstrated. Peripheral generality error, not a main-theorem counterexample.

checks.assessment: confirmed invalid contact-value step in general lemma; Minor retained
checks.independent_reasoning: Read source lines 1008-1038, Lemma 6.1. At a positive maximum m of u_k-Q_epsilon the test that touches from above is Q_epsilon+m; the displayed F uses Q_epsilon itself in the zero-order slot. The lemma states continuous ellipticity with no uniform ellipticity or zero-order monotonicity restriction that saves this step. For F(M,p,z,x)=(tr M)^5+z and u_k=u=Q=0, the actual evaluation at x=0 is (2n epsilon)^5-epsilon^4. In n=4, epsilon=1/65536 gives exactly -1/36893488147419103232<0, checked with Fraction arithmetic in this session; F is continuous and monotone in the matrix order. The annulus inequalities and positive interior maximum hold for this small epsilon. No failure of the stability theorem itself follows.
checks.counterevidence_and_severity: Adding m to the test restores contact. Since 0<m<=||u_k-u||infinity+epsilon^4, m tends to zero and continuity gives the intended limit. The actual application source 899 and 911-915 is a pure Hessian operator G_H(M)=tr(M+H)-sqrt(2+|M+H|^2), independent of the zero-order argument, so this omission does not break that application or establish a false main Hessian theorem. Minor is retained.
